title: "Day 5 — Architecture Integration and Final Project"
format: html
---

For four days you built the pieces one at a time: a lakehouse that stores
data reliably (Day 1), a streaming layer that gets it there in real time
(Day 2), a vector index and RAG pipeline that lets an AI system reason over
it (Day 3), and a quality/governance/lineage layer that keeps the whole thing
trustworthy and auditable (Day 4). Each of those days was deliberately
self-contained — its own notebook, its own tools, its own narrow problem.

**Today has no new tool to learn.** Day 5 is where those four pieces stop
being four separate labs and become one system. The technical question
changes from "how does Kafka work" or "how does a vector index work" to "how
do these things hand data to each other, in what order, and what happens when
one of them fails or flags bad data." That's a systems-design question, not a
new-library question — which is exactly the skill a production AI platform
actually demands, and exactly what the capstone grades.

The practical skills the day is built around: combining all of this week's
components into one architecture, building a scalable AI data system out of
them, **presenting the architectural decisions behind that system**, and
**simulating an enterprise production environment** rather than a one-off
notebook demo.

The second half of today is the **final project**: a single starter notebook
that already runs end-to-end using lightweight stand-ins for every one of the
week's real tools, and your team's job — in teams of three — is to replace
those stand-ins with the real Kafka, Delta Lake, Great Expectations, and
vector-DB code you already built earlier in the week.

## Subtopics for today

1. The unified reference architecture — how ingestion, storage, quality,
   governance, and RAG serving connect into one platform
2. The recommended technology stack for each architectural layer
3. AI infrastructure orchestration — coordinating compute, workflows, models,
   and data at platform scale (Airflow DAGs and beyond)
4. The final capstone project — structure, the team extension checklist, and
   the grading rubric
5. **Hands-on lab:** the Day 5 capstone starter — a runnable five-module
   pipeline your team extends into the real thing

Read [The Unified Architecture](01_unified_architecture.qmd), then
[The Final Project](02_final_project.qmd), then work through the
[lab notebook](Day5_Lab.ipynb) — it *is* the starting point for your capstone
submission, not just a demo to read.
